newsitem.title: USA: EA sees contract manufacturing profits.
newsitem.headline: EA sees contract manufacturing profits.

text.p: EA Industries Inc said Monday its directors had adopted a plan to refocus the company on its core business of contract manufacturing and it expects to be profitable in 1997 as a result.
EA said it expects to fund the business by leveraging the Aydin Corp shares it holds and by limiting future funding of BarOn Technologies and the Israel Aircraft Industries joint venture.
It said Chairman Irwin Gross has agreed to provide bridge financing of $1 million until the plan has been fully implemented.
This $1 million loan is in addition to the $2.1 million of notes Gross purchased in August, a company spokesman said.

EA said the loan will be used to finance additional equipment purchases needed to support growth of its contract manufacturing subsidiary Tanon Manufacturing Inc and to provide working capital for EA and Tanon.
Revenue from contract manufacturing increased to $77.1 million in 1995 from $30.5 million in 1994, and revenues for the first half of 1996 increased 23 percent from the first half of 1995.

Based on a review of forecasts of current customers, together with orders from new customers, the company said, it believes Tanon's revenue growth in 1997 should exceed the industry average growth rate of 22 percent.
EA also said it estimates the breakeven level for its contract manufacturing operations varies from about $90 million to $100 million, depending on the mix of business.
Based on current estimates, it said, Tanon expects to cross the breakeven level in 1997 and be profitable for the year.

Tanon expects to complete the previously announced acquisition of Tri-Star Technologies Inc in the fourth quarter. This would result in significant additional revenue and net income for Tanon in 1997, beyond the expectations mentioned above, EA said.

It said it had agreed to loan BarOn up to $900,000 during the fourth quarter. Additional financing for BarOn will be provided by conducting an initial public offering, a private placement, or a strategic partnership by BarOn.

EA has provided some $7.5 million in financing for its joint venture with Israel Aircraft Industries. EA and its partners FIBI Holding Co, United Mizrahi Bank Ltd and Tamarix Capital Corp expect to establish a venture fund in the first quarter of 1997 to provide any additional capital needed for the joint venture.
As previously reported, EA has terminated merger discussions with Aydin. EA said it continues to hold shares of Aydin with a market value of about $6 million.
EA is holding such shares as an investment but may borrow against them, sell a portion of them, or use this asset in another fashion, it said.
